paper.title: ATOM3D: Tasks On Molecules in Three Dimensions
paper.authors: Raphael J. L. Townshend, Martin Vögele, Patricia Suriana et al.

thesis: Our results indicate that many molecular problems stand to gain from three-dimensional molecular learning, and that there is potential for improvement on many tasks which remain underexplored.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: How can the target scientific task be compared under fixed data and evaluation rules?

nodes.title: Freeze tasks and metrics
nodes.body: To lower the barrier to entry and facilitate further developments in the field, we also provide a comprehensive suite of tools for dataset processing, model training, and evaluation in our open-source atom3d Python package.

nodes.title: Evaluate reference systems
nodes.body: To address this, we present ATOM3D, a collection of both novel and existing benchmark datasets spanning several key classes of biomolecules.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: The specific choice of architecture proves to be critical for performance, with three-dimensional convolutional networks excelling at tasks involving complex geometries, graph networks performing well on systems requiring detailed positional information, and the more recently developed equivariant networks showing significant promise.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Our results indicate that many molecular problems stand to gain from three-dimensional molecular learning, and that there is potential for improvement on many tasks which remain underexplored.
